findings.reason: The conformance route named in the scenario is blocked (apiTarget is a lookup in the hard-coded API_MAP, so an unlisted entity is skipped), but the compat route is open: the catalog's source label is the contract's own `domain` field, and resolveRoles' literal publisher/consumer fallback resolves roles for ANY entity whose two variants declare `domain: publisher` and `domain: consumer`; the raw schema[0].name then reaches the describe() string and the file path, and writeArtifactTree joins it with no containment check. §3.9 tests are never withheld (R-129), so the file is written.

findings.reason: readPath returns the stored value for a present key, so `taskId: null` yields null (not undefined) and the guard at plan.ts:258 passes; PLAN_SCHEMA constrains payload only to `type: object`; no adversary rule inspects the correlation value (vacuity (g) only checks tautological assertions); the emitted find compares with `===`, so a consumer record whose matchOn is null, or whose parent path is null (at() returns the null intermediate), is selected. The false green additionally needs the publisher to accept the null payload value and such a consumer record to exist, which is live state.

findings.reason: The loop sleeps a full pollIntervalSeconds after every miss, including one that happens with less than an interval left before the deadline, so pollUntil can return up to pollIntervalSeconds after timeoutSeconds; the Vitest budget is timeoutSeconds + 30 s and plan.ts allows pollIntervalSeconds up to timeoutSeconds, so for interval > 30 the generic Vitest timeout fires first (and the trigger request already consumed part of the budget).

findings.reason: The case-sensitive compare at emit.ts:132 is real, but the stated scenario (literal "String" against a contract that declares "string") never reaches emission: the adversary's wireType is also case-sensitive, so the literal contradicts the contract, is flagged R-133a Critical, and the plan is withheld. The emitted check can only be unpassable when the contract's own logicalType is non-lowercase, which the ODCS enum marks invalid; functional-gen.ts feeds invalid entries into grounding without filtering and schema-model.ts keeps the raw casing, so that route exists in code, but whether any such contract is in the catalog cannot be told from the repo.

The crawl's in-source collision check is keyed by contract id only, so two files with different ids and the same schema[0].name are both cataloged under one source; generateArtifacts pushes one conformance entry per contract while the path uses only source and entity, and the stable sort keeps #0 before #1 so writeArtifactTree's second write overwrites the first; the compat pair is picked with `find` over a catalog built from an unsorted DynamoDB Scan.

findings.reason: fileSlug drops everything before the last `/` of the canonical id, so `awp-app-plane/CRE-R-24` and `jira-awp/CRE-R-24` map to the same path; emitFunctionalTests orders by natural id (awp-app-plane first) and writeFunctionalArtifactTree writes each file in that order with no collision check, so the later one overwrites. Nothing in the code prevents the precondition (a second source label already exists in the live catalog, OQ-17), though no such colliding pair is shown to exist today; R-117d mandates the bare-id name, so the defect is the missing collision guard, not the naming.

notes: Finding 0: the scenario's conformance example (`conformance/<source>.../../x`) is gated — apiTarget (packages/core/src/api-map.ts:101 `return API_MAP[source]?.[entity];`) returns undefined for an unlisted entity and the contract is skipped. The live route is compat via author-set `domain: publisher` / `domain: consumer` (refresh.ts:106 + api-map.ts:93-94), which yields `compat/<raw name>.generated.test.ts`.

New (not in findings): `API_MAP[source]?.[entity]` (api-map.ts:101) and `flows[entity]` (api-map.ts:89) are plain-object lookups, so an entity named `constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty` etc. resolves to an inherited Object.prototype member; apiTarget then returns a truthy function and generateArtifacts pushes a conformance entry whose target.path/recordsAt/baseUrlEnv are undefined (emit.ts:17 renders `const recordsAt = undefined;`). The flows lookup falls through harmlessly because flow.publisher is undefined.

New (not in findings): the contract id (`doc.id`, packages/core/src/metadata.ts:46, unsanitised) is interpolated into `//` comment lines at packages/testgen/src/emit.ts:19 and :76-77; a line break inside `id` would end the comment and the remainder becomes code. Not traced whether an id containing a newline survives the catalog key path (entrySk) and the read API URL.

Finding 4: packages/functions/src/functional-gen.ts:78-82 builds ContractInput[] from every listEntries() row with no `validation` filter, so ODCS-invalid contracts do reach functional grounding; this is the only route by which a non-lowercase logicalType can reach the model and pass the adversary's case-sensitive check.
